fatal_errors: The proposed quench-and-age intervention does not reconstruct spark plasma sintering of ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder at 800–1000 °C.
The 250–350 °C aging regime omits the relevant 1000 °C sintering condition, 900 °C air-oxidation test, and 3.5 wt% NaCl corrosion test.
The hypothesized CSRO/spinodal pathway is not supported by evidence from Mg-containing alloys; the principal cited study concerns a PdAgCuAuPtZn precious-metal alloy.
The response replaces the required lower-temperature sintered comparison with an as-cast baseline and even suggests a different Al-Cu-Si-Zn-Mg alloy family.
It misses the dense microstructure and uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases, as well as passive-film blocking of chloride penetration and biphasic parabolic oxidation kinetics.
The stated boundaries do not address inadequate densification below about 800 °C or Mg volatilization above 1000 °C.
explanation: The hypothesis is internally testable and offers a clear microscopy-based falsification rule, but it addresses a substantially different alloy-processing problem. Its main agreement with the target is limited to the broad ideas that a metastable solid solution may transform into intermetallic-containing structures and that this evolution can affect corrosion and oxidation. It fails to identify SPS, the correct thermal and service conditions, densification, oxide barrier phases, passive-film behavior, parabolic oxidation kinetics, or the optimal properties at 1000 °C. The evidence discipline is especially weak because the cited spinodal/CSRO evidence is from an unrelated precious-metal MPEA rather than a reported Mg-containing alloy.
